entities.summary:
The Prague offensive was the last major military operation on the eastern front during World War II, taking place in Prague, Czechoslovakia, from May 6 to 11, 1945. Led by the Soviet Red Army, the operation aimed to capture the city of Prague and bring an end to the war in Europe. The offensive was a decisive moment in the war, as it led to the surrender of German forces in Prague and the liberation of the city from Nazi occupation.

The Prague offensive was a culmination of the Soviet Union's advance into Eastern Europe, which began in 1944 with the Warsaw Uprising. The operation involved a massive force of Soviet troops, who launched a multi-pronged attack on German positions in and around Prague. The city was heavily damaged during the fighting, but the Soviet victory marked a significant turning point in the war.

The consequences of the Prague offensive were far-reaching. The city of Prague was finally liberated from Nazi rule, and the Soviet Union was able to secure a significant victory in Europe. The operation also marked the beginning of the Soviet Union's occupation of Eastern Europe, which would have a profound impact on the region's politics and society in the years to come.

As one historian noted, 'The Prague offensive was a turning point in the war, marking the beginning of the end of Nazi Germany's dominance in Europe.' The operation remains an important moment in the history of World War II, and its legacy continues to be felt to this day.
